the bond reliability is determined by the Au–Al corrosion in the bond interface and the corrosion rate depends on the resin compound, impurities in gold and the Au–Al reaction products.
the thermal reliability of Au–Al bonds encapsulated in resin is strongly influenced by the resin compounds, gold wire and intermetallic compounds.
the Au/Al bonds encapsulated in the resin compound are thermally unstable and therefore should not be used for high temperature operation.

the Au–Al corrosion reaction is the major cause for the thermal failure at Au/Al wire bonding.
it is necessary to select the proper resin compounds and gold wire materials to insure the thermal stability of Au/Al bond in bi-phenly epoxy resin.

the thermal reliability of gold–aluminum bonds is strongly affected by the intermetallic compounds and their growth kinetics, which is in turn controlled by the resin compound and gold–wire impurities.

the Au/Al bond reliability is strongly affected by the resin compound and the gold wire material, and the use of alloyed gold wire was effective for the improvement of the bond reliability.
the use of the alloy wire is an effective means to improve the bond reliability.
the Au/Al bond degradation can be suppressed by using alloyed gold wire with the low Br content in molding resin.
